title: Obsessive-compulsive: the urge and the effort to resist
description: In obsessive-compulsive disorder, a trigger, such as touching something that might be dirty, brings an intrusive thought and a strong urge to do something about it, such as washing or checking. The episode follows that moment, as studied by showing people with OCD things that bring on their symptoms.
caveat: The findings come from a pooled analysis of studies that deliberately provoked symptoms in a scanner, comparing provocation with neutral periods within people with OCD rather than comparing them with people without OCD, and a second pooled analysis that found consistent differences in the same circuits without, in the part read, giving a direction. The order of events is reconstructed: the scans average over the provocation period. That the frontal and parietal activity reflects effort to resist the urge is the authors' suggestion, not something measured. OCD takes different forms in different people, and researchers link those forms to partly different circuits.

phases.name: A trigger
phases.caption: Something sets off the intrusive thought, for example a reminder of contamination or of something left unchecked.

phases.name: The urge
phases.caption: The circuits running from the orbitofrontal cortex and the anterior cingulate through the striatum become active. This is the most consistent finding when symptoms are provoked.

order.rationale: The studies compare whole provocation periods with neutral ones. That the urge follows the trigger is how the task is built.

phases.name: Trying to resist
phases.caption: A network on the left, including the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and the precuneus, is also active. The researchers suggest this may reflect the effort to resist the urge.

order.rationale: This network was active during the same provocation periods. Placing it after the urge follows the authors' suggestion that it reflects resisting, which was not measured as a separate step.

phases.name: Afterwards
phases.caption: The urge eases, whether or not it was acted on. What the brain does at this point was not studied in the sources read; this last part is an assumption.

order.rationale: No source read followed the end of a provoked episode. The return to rest is assumed.

regions.explanation: Part of the circuit most consistently active when OCD symptoms are provoked, in a pooled analysis. A second pooled analysis found consistent differences in the circuit linking the orbitofrontal cortex and the striatum, without a direction in the abstract, and notes that results have not been entirely consistent.
